To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the evolution of catalytic function can be explained by the interplay of epistatic interactions in the genetic background and the effects of dominant mutations that are constrained by the physical structure of the protein.
epistasis is pervasive and that it constrains the evolution of protein function.

1) epistasis can be quantified and used to identify key residues that contribute to the evolution of enzyme function; 2) epistasis is the result of the interdependence of residues in protein structure and can be used to infer past evolutionary events that have led to enzyme function; and 3) epistasis constrains the evolution of enzyme structure and function, but also provides a mechanism to generate novel function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanistic basis of epistasis and its effects on the evolution of catalytic function.
understanding how epistasis constrains the emergence and divergence of protein function in specialized metabolism.
the emergence of new function in enzymes, and the evolution of new metabolic functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
epistasis is an essential component in the evolution of protein function.
epistasis can constrain the effects of otherwise seemingly dominant mutations.
the evolution of enzyme function, and by extension, the emergence and specialization of metabolic pathways are constrained by epistasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the emergence and divergence of terpene synthesis in plants is the result of epistasis, and the evolution of terpene metabolism is an excellent example of the constraining effects of epistasis on enzyme function.

the evolution of terpene synthesis is an excellent model for understanding the evolution of enzyme function and that the study of enzyme evolution is a useful model for understanding the forces of evolution in general.
epistasis is not only a pervasive force in biology but also a powerful tool for understanding evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dominance and epistatic interactions are not only a feature of evolution, but also a tool that can be harnessed to understand the mechanistic basis of enzyme function.
the physical basis for many epistatic interactions is not a mystery.
epistasis is an essential component of enzyme evolution and is not a nuisance to overcome but a fundamental process to be understood.
